attrs.evidence: None. GPT-5.6's correction to R7, and it is the half of EMB-LINEAGE-WORKLIST that R7 got wrong. R7 imported the under-inclusion result from open software ecosystems — Rasheed et al. on hidden dependencies — and treated it as an inherent property of lineage. It is not: it is a property of ecosystems where a build can read undeclared inputs. A CLOSED, MEDIATED factory can attempt the opposite by construction — every admitted derivation reads only through mediated handles, every mediated read records a typed support edge, every output commits only if its support edges are sealed in its receipt, and no ambient filesystem, network, model or tool read may influence an admitted artifact without appearing in support. Bazel's sandboxed, hermetic actions are the industrial demonstration that the discipline is achievable for builds. Whether it is achievable for a world whose transitions include model inference is the open question, and it is a better research target than importing today's SBOM limitations into the architecture.
attrs.gap: SUPERSEDED AT R7.2 BY SUPPORT-CHANNEL-COMPLETE, and NOT renamed. GPT-5.6 ruled that this record's wording is either too strong (`every semantic dependency` demands mechanistic attribution) or too coarse (an untyped closure is conservative for nothing in particular). A claim_id preserves proposition identity, so the successor is a new record and this one keeps its sentence. Demoted rather than refuted: nothing showed it false, and what it named is simply not the property worth pursuing.

attrs.review_focus: The hard case is model inference: an admitted artifact produced with a model in the loop depends on the model's weights and its context, and `mediated handle` has to cover both for this to be more than a build-system property.
attrs.statement: In a world that mediates every admitted transition, every semantic dependency of an admitted artifact is represented by a typed support edge.
